title: Parse nanosecond-precision timestamps in parseRFC3339 (Greptile P1, re-review)
rationale: On Greptile's re-review, a P1 remained: parseRFC3339 used time.RFC3339, which fails on timestamps with fractional seconds. Google Cloud APIs serialize google.protobuf.Timestamp with nanosecond precision (e.g. "2026-06-01T00:00:00.000000000Z"), so every interval/sampleTime data point (steps, distance, heart rate, exercise) would silently fail to parse and be dropped from the local store, leaving trends/streaks/correlate operating on a truncated dataset with no user-visible error.

changes.summary: parseRFC3339 now tries time.RFC3339Nano first (parses both fractional and whole-second timestamps), falling back to time.RFC3339. Fractional-second timestamps now extract instead of being silently dropped.
changes.validated_outcome: go build/vet pass; new TestExtractPoint/nanosecond-precision_timestamps_extract case passes (would fail before the fix).

changes.summary: Added a regression subtest asserting that steps (interval) and weight (sampleTime) rows with .000000000Z / .123456789Z fractional seconds extract successfully.
changes.validated_outcome: go test -count=1 ./internal/health/ -run TestExtractPoint passes all subtests.
